description:
FILED s464aw while shipping #972 (which covered the arithmetic, string,
comparison and bitwise families).  These are the operators perl overloads
that PCL still never asks about.  Probed 5.40.3, one class per row, against a
class with `0+', `""' and a `nomethod' key so the divergence is visible:

    abs $x     perl nomethod(op=abs)     PCL 7        (numifies via 0+)
    sqrt $x    perl nomethod(op=sqrt)    PCL 2.6457â¦
    atan2($x,2) perl nomethod(op=atan2)  PCL 1.2924â¦
    $x x 2     perl the `x' handler      PCL stringifies (autogeneration only)

and by the same reading `cos' `sin' `exp' `log' `!' are unasked.  Note that
`int' is NOT in this list: perl autogenerates it from `0+' and PCL's
numification is already perl's answer (probed identical).

The three-way split matters when writing the fix:
  * `x' HAS a correct autogeneration in PCL (it stringifies, which is perl's
    answer for a class with no `x' key), so it needs the HANDLER lookup only;
  * `abs' perl autogenerates from `<' and `-', not from `0+' -- so PCL's `0+'
    answer is wrong even before nomethod;
  * `sqrt'/`cos'/`sin'/`exp'/`log'/`atan2' have NO autogeneration at all.
Each therefore has a different correct fall-through, and a single "just add
the lookup" pass over the family would be wrong for `abs'.

`%with-unary-overload' (added by #972) is the shape for the unary ones;
`%with-binary-overload' for `x' and `atan2'.

BAR: the probe rows above plus the autogeneration matrix per operator (a
class with only `-'+`<' for abs, etc.); the sweep; guards in
Pl/t/overload-01.t.

=== DONE (s470bk) ===
FIXED, runtime-only, in two commits: the `x` half rode with #1001(a) (which
needed something for `x=` to delegate to), the rest in its own.

THE TASK'S THREE-WAY SPLIT WAS RIGHT, and each member got its own spelling:
  * `sqrt cos sin exp log` (unary) + `atan2` (binary): NO autogeneration, so
    `%with-unary-overload` / `%with-binary-overload` as they stand â own
    handler, else `nomethod`, else the numeric body.
  * `x`: the HANDLER LOOKUP only, `:autogenerated t`, because perl derives `x`
    from `""` and PCL's body already was that answer.
  * `!`: `%with-unary-overload` gained the `:autogenerated` key its binary twin
    has had since #972.  PCL already answered the derivation right (p-true-p
    runs the `bool` conversion chain), so only the OWN handler was missing.
  * `abs`: a THIRD order â own -> AUTOGENERATE from `<` and `-` (perl's
    `$x < 0 ? -$x : $x`, honouring `fallback => 0`'s prohibition) -> `nomethod`
    -> body.  Its own function, `%p-abs-overload`.  A single "just add the
    lookup" pass really would have been wrong here.
  * `int` stays ABSENT, probed: perl derives it from `0+` and PCL's
    numification is already that answer.

RULE 11 side effect: `p-not` and `p-!` were two copies of
`(if (p-true-p a) "" 1)`.  perl's `not` is `!` with a different precedence and
NO separate overload key, so `p-not` calls `p-!` and there is one reading.

MEASURED: 27 rows one file (scratch/s470bk/pov/m1005.pl), 9 identical before ->
**25 after**.  The two residues are exactly #1006(b) (a `fallback => 0` class
must reach `nomethod` for `.` and `x`), which stays declined with its own
measurement.

`p-<` and `p--` were added to the runtime's existing forward-declaim block
because `%p-abs-overload` calls them 4000 lines above their defuns; a BARE
forward reference prints a compile warning, and four gate files CAPTURE output.

Gate 203/6866.  Guard `Pl/t/overload-01.t` 37 -> 40 rows (rows 38-40),
inverse-verified on a `92a568e` worktree; row 40 carries the negatives and
passes both ways by design.
subject: abs/sqrt/cos/sin/exp/log/atan2/x/! have no `use overload` dispatch
